statement.quote: This coursework assesses your ability to evaluate supervised learning models in a setting where the most obvious measure of success is misleading. It contributes to learning outcomes 2 (evaluate and compare predictive models using an appropriate methodology) and 4 (communicate technical findings to a non-specialist audience) in the module descriptor. The emphasis is on the quality of your about...

Your report should open by framing the prediction problem in your own terms and describing the supplied data in enough detail for a reader to follow the decisions that come later. Write this opening for a reader from the operations team rather than for a machine learning specialist.

Particular attention should be paid to the class imbalance in the outcome: because missed appointments are comparatively rare, the report should consider how this affects the way the models are trained as well as the way their performance is judged.

The evaluation measures you report should be chosen deliberately and justified by the practical cost of each kind of error in this setting; a model defended on its accuracy alone will not be regarded as adequately evaluated. Marks in this part of the report reward explanation more than the number of measures reported.

Your discussion should compare at least two different modelling approaches, with final performance reported on a held-out test set that played no part in model selection or tuning. Cross-validation on the training data is a sensible way to choose between settings, but its results are not a substitute for the final held-out comparison.

The report should close with a critical reflection on the limitations of your evaluation and on the further work you would recommend before any model was used to select patients for reminder calls. In that reflection, consider whether any choice made during training could have leaked information into the test results. Any resampling or class weighting must be applied to the training data only.

Your specification must include 1. A focused research question. 2. The aims and objectives of the project. 3. A short review of related work, citing at least eight sources. 4. The proposed methodology, including how you will obtain your data. 5. Ethical considerations and the ethics review route you will follow. 6. A timeline to the final submission, for example as a Gantt chart.
Marking: Specifications are marked pass or fail with written feedback; a failed specification must be revised and resubmitted within 10 working days.
